message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude, and we were on a lease. When the lease was ending, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, leaving only the last bit of his half of the rent and a few things he mentioned in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and that cost comes out of your deposit. I've heard of cases where people have $250 taken off their deposit just for someone to take three milk crates of stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off. So, I texted and emailed him for two weeks asking him to pick up his stuff or let me take them to the dump, but he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I figured I'd sell them. There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party he was at, and we were being polite. He asked how the move-out was, and I said it was good. Naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games, and I told him that I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did, but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Alright, so to figure this out, I need to consider a few things. First, what were the terms of the lease? Did it specify what happens to belongings left behind? Second, did I make reasonable efforts to contact him about his stuff? Third, was selling the games the best course of action, or should I have handled it differently? I think the lease probably had standard terms, but I'm not sure. If it said that the landlord can dispose of belongings, then legally, I was in the right to get rid of his stuff. But ethically, is that the right thing to do? I mean, he left without giving much notice, and he didn't respond to my messages. So, I tried to contact him, but he didn't respond. Selling the games for $600 seems like a good thing because it's money that could have been lost if the landlord had to dispose of them. But he's upset because he feels like I took his stuff without his permission. Even though legally I wasn't wrong, maybe I should have handled it differently. Maybe I should have held onto the games longer or tried to contact him through another method, like a phone call, instead of just texting and emailing. Or perhaps I should have stored the games somewhere safe until he could pick them up. But I didn't have the space or the means to store 60 games for an indefinite period. On the other hand, he left without giving much notice and didn't respond to my attempts to contact him. So, in a way, he abandoned his stuff, and I was just following the rules to prevent the landlord from charging me for disposal. I'm also thinking about the value of the games. $600 is a significant amount, and he might feel like he lost out on that money. But legally, since he didn't respond, I don't think I have to give him any of that money. But is it the right thing to do? Should I offer him some of the money as a goodwill gesture, even though I'm not legally obligated? That might help mend our relationship, but I don't know if he'd accept it. Overall, I think I did what I had to do to protect myself from losing money on the deposit, but I can see why he's upset. Maybe I could have communicated better or found another way to handle his belongings. But given the circumstances, I don't think I'm the asshole for selling his games.
